nl.statement: The observed-data experiment for a lower-threshold modified treatment policy. The baseline-stratum space is finite, \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,J\}\); the treatment is continuous, \(A\in[0,1]\); the outcome is bounded, \(Y\in[0,1]\); and the observed unit is \(O=(X,A,Y)\), with \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) drawn independently from one law \(P\). Each \(P\) carries the stratum masses \(p_x=P(X=x)\), a Borel conditional treatment density \(\pi_x\) with \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\), and a continuous outcome regression \(\mu_x^P\) that is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\). The lower-threshold clamp \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) produces the conditional atom mass \(q_x(\delta)=\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\), the retained natural-course mean \(\nu_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]\), and the observed-data target \(\theta_\delta(P)=\nu_\delta(P)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)\). The finite-stratum clamp model \(\mathcal M\) is the class of laws satisfying the conditional-density, stratum-mass, polynomial-thinning, and Hölder member conditions. — Emitted in Basic.lean as `ClampObs` (X : Fin J, A : Real, B : Real carrier for Y, exactly the DoseObs/DoseLaw idiom of CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DoseResponseMinimax_Research/Basic.lean:58-106) and `ClampLaw` (fields dataMeasure, px, pi, mu). Every consumer reads these unassumed, because `P : ClampLaw` binds every statement of the plan; strict positivity `0 < p_x` is then `px_eq` plus `ass:stratum-mass` plus `0 < p_min` from the S2 `RegimeConstants`. The deterministic regime constants and rate objects of the frontier. Known Hölder exponent \(\beta>0\) with local-polynomial order \(\ell=\lfloor\beta\rfloor\) (and \(\ell=\beta-1\) when \(\beta\) is an integer) and known radius \(L>0\); known thinning exponent \(\kappa\geq0\) with density comparison constants \(0<c_-\leq\kappa+1\leq c_+\); stratum-probability floor \(p_{\min}\in(0,1/J]\); threshold envelope \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\); prespecified noncoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\); and an arbitrary deterministic threshold sequence \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\). Attached to these are the information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\), the candidate frontier \(r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\), the two phase scales \(\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}=n^{-1/[2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)]}\) and \(\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\), and the two observed-data performance criteria \(R_n^\star=\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)|\) and \(L_n^\star\), the worst-case expected length among intervals with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\). Deterministic at this same level is the calibration multiplier \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\), a function of the prespecified noncoverage level and the number of strata alone, which sets the test radius of both the bias-aware interval and the exact-modulus handle. — Plain real/nat regime parameters plus real-valued rate sequences. Declared spaces are ENFORCED by one standing well-formedness predicate `RegimeConstants beta kappa L cminus cplus pmin deltaBar alpha` (0<beta, 0<=kappa, 0<L, 0<c_- <= kappa+1, kappa+1 <= c_+, p_min in (0,1/J], deltaBar in (0,1), alpha in (0,1/2)) threaded into every lemma/theorem, exactly the `RegimeConstants` idiom at CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DoseResponseMinimax_Research/Basic.lean:334; the threshold-sequence membership delta_n in [0,deltaBar] is a separate threaded `ThresholdSequence` predicate because delta_n is a SEQUENCE, and `ell` is defined as `ellOf beta` (the note's floor convention with the integer correction). h_n and r_n are realized by def:bandwidth / def:frontier; delta_crit, delta_edge, R_n^star, L_n^star have no core definition node and are realized by this block's own `deltaCrit`, `deltaEdge`, `observedMinimaxRisk`, `observedMinimaxLength` defs in Basic.lean. The realized-design local-polynomial experiment inside one baseline stratum. The sample is split into three deterministic blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) with \(|I_j|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\). Writing \(U_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\) and \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top\), the design carries the normalized reference moment matrices \(M_{\kappa,\rho}=\{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}/\{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}\) with uniform constant \(\lambda_\star=(c_-/c_+)\inf_{\rho\geq0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\kappa,\rho})\), the local count \(N_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\delta_n\leq A_i\leq\delta_n+h_n\}\), the unnormalized Gram \(G_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top\), the good-design event \(\Omega_x=\{N_x>0,\ \lambda_{\min}(G_x)\geq\lambda_\star N_x/2\}\), and the exact intercept weights \(w_{ix}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), \(w_{ix}=0\) off it. From these are built the sample-split total-Gram-stabilized estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) and the bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) with its local atom fallback on singular-Gram events. The same realized design supports a candidate sharp radius. For a realized design \(z\) and an admissible affine weight vector \(w\) supported on the local window and reproducing every monomial through degree \(\ell\) at the threshold, \(\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)\) is the supremum of \(|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_if(A_i)-f(\delta_n)|\) over the \([0,1]\)-valued Hölder class \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\); \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) is the infimum over such \(w\) of that bias plus \(t(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2)^{1/2}\), totalized to zero when no admissible weight exists; \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) is its integral under the \(n\)-fold independent observed-design law; and \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t)\) is the supremum of that integral over \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). These are radius, or half-length, quantities; the zero value on an empty feasible set only totalizes the candidate, and no honesty, nondegeneracy or optimality of an interval using it is asserted here. The split itself may also be chosen as a sequence: an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\) determines every object above, and \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) denotes a sequence of such splits, which may depend on the deterministic threshold sequence but not on the realized data. — REVISION (round 5, reviewer flag FLAG-missed-reuse on S3). The structural full-data overlay carrying the causal target. On a standard Borel latent state space \(\mathcal U\) there is a latent response variable \(U\) and, for each \(x\in\mathcal X\), a jointly Borel measurable structural response map \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\); the potential-outcome process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\) is represented simultaneously outside one null set by \(Y(a)=g_X(a,U)\). A full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) governs \((X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})\) and has observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin \(P\); it carries the full-data response mean \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[g_x(a,U)\mid X=x]\) and the clamp-policy mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_\delta(A)\}]\). \[
\mathcal W_{z,x}=\left\{w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}: w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\quad \sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell\right\}.
\]
If \(V_{z,x}\) is the matrix whose row indexed by \(i\in S_{z,x}\) is \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\), these are equivalently the affine realized-design constraints \(V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0\), and the associated total Gram is \(G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}\).  Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) that are continuous and satisfy
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|\leq L|a'-a|^\beta
\quad\text{for every }a,a'\in[0,1],
\]
where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition.  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the exact realized Hölder bias and conditional radius objective by
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)\right|,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)+t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]

\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\

\end{cases}
\]

\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z),
\]

\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},\qquad
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)

\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]

Its \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\), and, within that member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) member conditions hold. \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfying the following memberwise structure relative to \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response space.)} Each member carries its own standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\) and an \(\mathcal U\)-valued random variable \(U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural response maps.)} Each member carries jointly Borel maps
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1],
\qquad x\in\mathcal X,
\]
and a jointly measurable potential-outcome process
\[
\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data law.)} Each member carries a probability law for
\[
(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\).
\item \textbf{(Causal member conditions.)} Within the member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) conditions hold.
\end{itemize}
The class is formed member by member, with membership determined on each member's own standard Borel carrier.

nl.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), the conditional pushforward law satisfies \(P\{d_\delta(A)\in\mathrm da\mid X=x\}=\pi_x(a)\mathbf 1\{a>\delta\}\,\mathrm da+q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(\mathrm da)\), with \(c_-\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\leq q_x(\delta)\leq c_+\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\).

Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfy \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and let \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) as in \cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}. Suppose the constants satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), \(L>0\), and \(0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)} \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and level.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation point.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Define the lower-tail atom mass
\[
q_x(\delta)=\int_{[0,\delta]}\pi_x(a)\,da .
\]
Then the conditional pushforward law of the clamped treatment satisfies
\[
P\{d_\delta(A)\in da\mid X=x\}
=
P\{A\in da,\ A\in(\delta,1]\mid X=x\}
+
q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(da),
\]
and the atom mass obeys
\[
\frac{c_-\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}
\leq
q_x(\delta)
\leq
\frac{c_+\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}.
\]

review.note: After unfolding the conditional measure, clamp, atom mass, and model predicates, the measure identity and both polynomial atom-mass bounds are equivalent to the paper statement on the declared domain.

nl.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(d_\delta(A)\) lies in the support of the conditional natural-treatment law given \(X=x\) almost surely. At \(\delta=0\) this follows from the identity map; at \(\delta>0\) every neighborhood of \(\delta\) has positive conditional probability by conditional absolute continuity and the lower polynomial envelope.

Let \(P\), \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\), \(x\), and \(\delta\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\).
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(J\ge 1\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\le \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\le 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum and threshold.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\le \delta\le \bar\delta\).

\[
0<\Pr_P(A\in U\mid X=x).
\]

nl.statement: Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\), let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be its observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin, and interpret \(\mathcal U\), \(U\), \(g_x\), and \(\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}\) as the carrier components packaged by this member. Consequently, for every \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(d_\delta(A)\) belongs to the support of the conditional natural-treatment law almost surely, \(Y\{d_\delta(A)\}=Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\) almost surely, and \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)=\theta_\delta(P)\).

\end{itemize}

\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),

P(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x,\ A\in B\}} Y\,dP^{\mathrm F}

\int_B m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\pi_x(a)\,da.

d_\delta(a)\in \operatorname{supp}\{\pi_x(a)\,da\text{ on }[0,1]\}

\]

\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad \kappa\geq0,\qquad L>0,\qquad c_->0,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\]
\[
p_{\min}>0,\qquad p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad 0<\alpha<\frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} The deterministic thresholds \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfy
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\]
for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} For each \(n\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks and
\[
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{0,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{1,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{2,n}|.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\), the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\), be as in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c<C\), depending only on the displayed regime constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, formed with split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta_n\), is observed-sample measurable, and the corresponding stabilized bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\), formed with the same split, order, bandwidth, and threshold, is an observed-sample measurable interval.

For the causal minimax criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria}, the same \(n\) also satisfies
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C r_n,
\]
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)
\leq C r_n,
\]
and, in the extended nonnegative-real order,
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}(c r_n)\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq \operatorname{ofReal}(C r_n).
\]

review.note: After unfolding the frontier, causal criteria, risks, coverage, expected length, estimator, and interval, Lean gives the same eventual uniform risk and honest-length chains with common positive finite constants; the minimax-length lower bound is equivalent to the stated lower bound for every uniformly honest observed-sample interval, and the measurability conjuncts express the advertised procedures' admissibility.

nl.statement:
Let \(S\) and \(T\) be standard Borel spaces and let \((Z,W)\) be an \(S\times T\)-valued random element.  There is a Borel probability kernel \(K:S\times\mathcal B(T)\to[0,1]\) such that, writing \(P_Z\) for the law of \(Z\),
\[
 \Pr\{Z\in B,W\in C\}=\int_B K(z,C)\,P_Z(\mathrm dz)
\]
for every Borel \(B\subseteq S\) and \(C\subseteq T\).

review.note: Lean is equivalent to the frozen rectangle-disintegration claim: arbitrary product laws are precisely laws of product-valued random elements, and the cited theorem implies this specialization with conditioning space S and target space T; source uniqueness is an unused stronger conjunct.

nl.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is exactly \(P\).  Thus the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M\) is surjective.  Moreover, for every \(n\) and every declared deterministic \(\delta_n\),
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star=R_n^\star
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star=L_n^\star.
\]
nl.frozen_body:
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(0<J\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\leq \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\), \(\kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) means that \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).
\item \textbf{(Full-data model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) means that \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class} with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is exactly \(P\). Hence the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M\) is surjective.

Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the causal frontier criteria in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria} satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta)=R_n^\star(\delta)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta,\alpha)=L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha).
\]
Here \(R_n^\star(\delta)\) is the infimum, over observed-measurable estimators with values in \([0,1]\), of the worst-case absolute-error risk over \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the observed clamp target at threshold \(\delta\), and \(L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha)\) is the infimum, over uniformly honest observed-measurable confidence procedures at level \(1-\alpha\), of the worst-case expected interval length over \(P\in\mathcal M\).

review.note: Modulo the source-matched regular-conditional-law carrier, Lean states exactly the observed-margin surjection and both criterion equalities for every n and every admissible deterministic threshold value; pointwise threshold quantification is equivalent to quantifying declared sequences.

nl.statement: If \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are independent random variables taking values in \([0,1]\), then, for every \(t>0\), \(\Pr\{|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m Z_i-m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E Z_i|>t\}\leq2\exp(-2mt^2)\).

review.note: Lean exactly encodes the frozen two-sided bound for independent measurable [0,1]-valued variables; the cited one-sided theorem applied to Z and -Z and combined by a union bound yields the stated constant and exponent.

nl.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), there is exactly one continuous function on \([0,\bar\delta]\) that is an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).  Hence \(\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P\) is well defined.
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) be a continuity-only observed clamp model with these constants, as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0\leq \kappa,\qquad
0<c_-,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Continuous versions.)} For \(r=1,2\), \(\mu_r:\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfies that \(a\mapsto \mu_r(x,a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Regression version property.)} For \(r=1,2\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X,A]=\mu_r(X,A)
\quad\text{\(P\)-almost surely.}
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\mu_1(x,a)=\mu_2(x,a)
\qquad\text{for every }a\in[0,\bar\delta].
\]

review.note: Existence is supplied by the unfolded ContClampModel hypothesis, while the quantified comparison of any two continuous conditional-expectation versions proves uniqueness on the full threshold interval and therefore makes the selected version well defined.

nl.statement:
Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) have observed margin \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\).  Then \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(a)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\), and, for every \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\),
\[
 \psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
 =\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]
 +\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(\delta)
 =\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P).
\]
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\), let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P^{\mathrm F}\) be a full-data law package with observed margin \(P\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data continuity model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) with constants \((\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(J>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), and \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\end{itemize}
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in\mathbb R\), define the full-data response mean by
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(a).
\]
Moreover, if
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\int Y\!\left(d_\delta(A)\right)\,dP^{\mathrm F},
\]
then, for every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P),
\]
where \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\) is the continuity-only clamp functional in \cref{obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional}.

review.note: After unfolding fullDataResponseMean, causalClampMean, contRegression, contClampFunctional, retainedMean, and atomMass, Lean states exactly the pointwise regression identity and the full equality chain ψδ(Pᴳ)=E_P[Y·1{A>δ}]+∑x p_x q_x(δ) μx,cont^P(δ)=θδ,cont(P) on δ∈[0,δ̄]; hPF supplies the stated model membership and observed margin, while hreg records the setup domains.

nl.statement:
The observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is surjective.  For every \(n\) and every declared deterministic \(\delta_n\), the observed-sample clamp-target criteria satisfy
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
 \qquad
 L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star.
\]
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that the continuity-regime design constants used in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria} hold for \((J,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), and that \(0<\alpha<1/2\).

Then the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is surjective: for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed margin is \(P\). Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the four continuity-frontier criteria of \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria}, evaluated at \((J,n,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\delta,\alpha)\), satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star .
\]

review.note: Lean states exactly the onto observed-margin map and the causal-versus-observed risk and length equalities for every n and every declared δ_n ∈ [0,δ̄]; hreg pins the core parameter spaces, and the explicit regular-conditional-law carrier is the exempt source-matched dependency.

nl.statement:
There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the declared model constants and on \(\alpha\), such that, for every deterministic \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c s_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
 \leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)|
 \leq Cs_n.
\]
The interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), has worst-case expected length at most \(Cs_n\), and every uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest interval has worst-case expected length at least \(cs_n\).  The same estimator and interval obey the corresponding causal statements over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\), and
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
 \qquad
 L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star.
\]
Consequently the continuity-only elbow is \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/[2(\kappa+1)]}\); at \(\delta_n=0\) the rate is \(n^{-1/2}\), whereas if \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), neither uniform risk consistency nor vanishing uniformly honest expected length is possible.
nl.frozen_body:
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose
\[
0<J,
\qquad
0\leq \kappa,
\qquad
0<c_-,
\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq \frac{1}{J},
\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,
\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12.
\]
Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<c<C\) such that the following statements hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Uniform frontier bounds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), and for every deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following bounds. With
\[
s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1},
\]
and with \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\), and \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\) as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria},
\[
c s_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
the interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\) has uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), its worst-case expected length is at most \(C s_n\), and
\[
c s_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star.
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\]
and the same estimator and interval satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
with causal coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) and causal worst-case expected length at most \(C s_n\).

\item \textbf{(Elbow and null-threshold rates.)} For the continuity-only rate in \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier},
\[
s_n\bigl(\delta_n=n^{-1/(2(\kappa+1))}\bigr)
\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
s_n(0)\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed positive thresholds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), and \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\),
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

review.note: After unfolding the model, criteria, estimator, interval, sampling, block, frontier, and asymptotic predicates, Lean states the same uniform eventual risk/coverage/length bounds, derives the causal lower bounds from the exact criterion equalities, and matches the elbow, zero-threshold, and fixed-positive-threshold clauses.

nl.statement: Let \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), and \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) be an admissible threshold sequence with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\) is attained as an interior balance root: \(0<h_n\), \(h_n\le1-\bar\delta\), and \(n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1\).  In particular the fallback branch of the bandwidth is eventually inactive, and \(\delta_n+h_n\le1\).
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(h_n\) denote the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} formed with \(\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Hölder exponent.)} The exponent \(\beta\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression} satisfies \(\beta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Polynomial-thinning exponent.)} The exponent \(\kappa\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} satisfies \(\kappa\geq0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold cap.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) is a deterministic real sequence satisfying \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
0<h_n,\qquad
h_n\leq 1-\bar\delta,\qquad
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1.
\]

review.note: The Lean lemma states exactly the eventual conjunction of positivity, the upper bound by \(1-\bar\delta\), and the exact balance identity for the information-balance bandwidth, which is the eventual-interior-root fact the prose attributes to the bandwidth definition.

nl.statement: Fix an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) with design constants \(\kappa\ge0\), \(0<c_-\le\kappa+1\le c_+\), and \(p_{\min}>0\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a threshold \(\delta\ge0\), and a window width \(h>0\) with \(\delta+h\le1\).  Write \(p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}=P\{X=x,\ 0\le(A-\delta)/h\le1\}\) for the population mass of the local window and \(\phi_j\) for the local monomial feature \(\{(A-\delta)/h\}^j\) restricted to that window.  Then the population localized Gram form is coercive with the uniform constant \(\lambda_\star\): for every \(v\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\), \[\lambda_\star p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2\le\sum_{j,k=0}^{\ell}v_jv_k\,\mathbb E_P\bigl[\mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le(A-\delta)/h\le1\}\phi_j\phi_k\bigr].\]
nl.frozen_body:
Fix an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with conditional-density, stratum-mass, and polynomial-thinning components as in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  Fix constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+\), and \(p_{\min}\), and a degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+>0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\delta\ge0\), \(h>0\), and \(\delta+h\le1\).
\end{itemize}
For an observation \(O=(X,A,Y)\), set
\[
p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\right],
\]
and, for \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\), define the local monomial feature
\[
\phi_j(O)
=
\mathbf 1\!\left\{0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\left(\frac{A-\delta}{h}\right)^j .
\]
Then, with \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) denoting the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, every \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_\star\,p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}
v_jv_k\,
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)
\right].
\]

review.note: The Lean lemma is the population localized-Gram coercivity with constant lambdaStar times the local-window mass, matching the displayed quadratic-form inequality on the local monomial features.

nl.statement: Fix a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\), an observed sample \(z\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a window width \(h>0\), and suppose \(\lambda_\star>0\) and that the good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds at \(z\).  Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \((w_{ix})_{i\in I_2}\) reproduce the monomials at the threshold, \(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}U_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\) for \(0\le j\le\ell\), and satisfy the two weight controls \[\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\le\frac{2\sqrt{\ell+1}}{\lambda_\star},\qquad \sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\le\frac{4(\ell+1)}{\lambda_\star^2N_x}.\]
nl.frozen_body:
Fix \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) with pairwise disjoint blocks satisfying \(|I_r|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(r=0,1,2\), an observed sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive bandwidth.)} \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive population Gram constant.)} The constant \(\lambda_\star\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Good local design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).
\end{itemize}
Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) and rescaled coordinates \(U_i\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfy, for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}.
\]
They also obey the two deterministic weight bounds
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
\le
\frac{2\sqrt{\ell+1}}{\lambda_\star},
\]
and, with \(N_x\) denoting the local count in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2
\le
\frac{4(\ell+1)}{\lambda_\star^2 N_x}.
\]

review.note: The Lean lemma delivers, on the good-Gram event, the monomial reproduction identity together with the explicit absolute-sum and square-sum weight bounds with the same constants as displayed.

nl.statement: Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be sampled independently with \(n\ge8\), fix a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and let \(\delta\ge0\) and \(h>0\) satisfy \(\delta+h\le1\), \(\lambda_\star>0\), and the balance equation \(n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa=1\).  Then the integrated square-root weight energy of the exact intercept weights obeys the explicit bound \[\int\Bigl(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\Bigr)^{1/2}dP^{\otimes n}\le\left[\frac{336\{4(\ell+1)/\lambda_\star^2\}}{p_{\min}c_-/(2\cdot2^\kappa)}\right]^{1/2}h^\beta,\] whose constant depends only on \(\ell,\kappa,\lambda_\star,p_{\min}\), and \(c_-\).  The bound combines the good-Gram weight-energy control, the lower bound on the local window mass, the split-block size, and the balance equation.
nl.frozen_body:
